aggregation.text_A: Most of the gain over a uniform split of the same per-round privacy comes from the aggregation weights that our allocation implies: 2.79 pp under the epsilon weights of Algorithm 2 and -0.18 pp when both use data-size weights. Accuracy claims are stated for Algorithm 2.
aggregation.text_B: When the strongest baseline also uses data-size weights, it is not below our method in every setting (-0.46 (alpha 0.1) / +0.57 (alpha 0.5) pp with data-size weights for both); the accuracy advantage is stated for the epsilon-weighted aggregation of Algorithm 2.
aggregation.text_C: Against CSRA with releases equal to the declared budgets, which release 5.4 times as much privacy per round as the 1/(N-k) adaptation, MFG-RegretNet is ahead under the epsilon weights of Algorithm 2 by +2.33 (alpha 0.1) / +0.99 (alpha 0.5) pp (development data, CIFAR-10, B=30; +0.13 (alpha 0.1) / +0.33 (alpha 0.5) pp with data-size weights for both).
